rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The couplet illustrates abandoning one’s own desire in favor of what the Beloved wills.
rows.anchor: أريد وصاله ويريد هجري . . . فأترك ما أؤيد لما يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Samiri led the people astray by summoning them to worship the calf; this was a kind of chastisement.
rows.anchor: بدعائه إياهم إلى عبادة العجل ، وهو نوع من التعزير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad returned from the ascension in expansive joy, bearing intimate prayer instructions and nearness for his companions, unlike Moses’ angry return.
rows.anchor: من المعراج بنعت البسط ، وجاء بالنجوى لأصحابه فيما أوجب الله عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses returned to his people angry and sorrowful and addressed them with reproach for breaking their promise.
rows.anchor: ورجع موسى إلى قومه بوصف الغضب والأسف ، وخاطبهم ببيان العتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people suspected their prophet of falsely making a promise; the ill omen of that suspicion led them to abandon the covenant and associate partners with God.
rows.anchor: ظنوا بنبيهم ظن السوء في خلقه الوعد ، فلحقهم شؤم ذلك حتى زاغوا عن العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who does not fulfill a covenant risks entering the same downward course.
rows.anchor: وكذلك يكون الأمر إذا لم يف المرء بعقده ، فإنه ينخرط في هذا السلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: They said they had not intended or understood the outcome; the Samiri fashioned the calf from ornaments taken from the Copts.
rows.anchor: لم نكن في ابتداء حالنا قاصدين إلى ما حصل منا ، ولا عالمين بما آلت إليه عاقبة حالنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forbidden wealth they had borrowed from the Copts bore an ill consequence and became a cause of calf worship.
rows.anchor: كانت الغنيمة وأموال المشركين حراما عليهم ، فاستعاروا الحلي من القبط ، وآل إليهم ما كان في أيديهم من الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pursuing worldly goods by unlawful means endangers the thinness of one’s religion.
rows.anchor: من انهمك في طلب الدنيا من غير وجه حلال يكون على خطر من رقة دينه

rows.speaker: يقال
rows.claim: After seeing idol worshippers, the Israelites asked Moses for a god like theirs; because their idol resembled a calf and the inclination was already hidden in their hearts, the Samiri made that shape.
rows.anchor: لما مروا على قوم يعبدون أصناما لهم قالوا لموسى : اجعل لنا إلها كما لهم آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Latent passions settled in the heart can lead to hidden association unless spiritual struggle cuts them out.
rows.anchor: خفايا الهوى إذا استكنت في القلب فما لم ينقش ذلك الشرك بمنقاش المنازلة

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: Israel accepted calf worship during Moses’ forty-day absence, whereas Muhammad’s community regarded even one anthropomorphic statement as a grave offense despite his much longer absence.
rows.anchor: خرج من بين أمته أربعين يوما برضي قومه بعبادة العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier communities altered the scripture entrusted to them, while God promised to preserve this Book and make it prevail over religion.
rows.anchor: استحفظوا كتابهم فبدلوه تبديلا ، بينما ضمن الحق - سبحانه - إعزاز هذا الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The calf could not answer them; one without speech, or power over harm and benefit, does not deserve worship.
rows.anchor: من لا قول له لا يتكلم ، ومن لا يملك الضر والنفع لا يستحق العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage rebuts those who deny that God possessed speech eternally or deny His power over good and evil.
rows.anchor: رد على من لم يثبت له في الأزل القول ، ولم يصفه بالقدرة على الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites failed to preserve Moses’ command even though he outranked Aaron.
rows.anchor: إنهم لم يحفظوا أمر موسى وهو فوق هارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If someone will not preserve the command of a higher-ranking person, how will he obey one of lower rank?
rows.anchor: من لم يحفظ أمر من هو أعلى رتبة يحفظ كيف أمر من هو أدنى منزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever abandons God’s right cannot be expected to respect shaykhs or other people’s rights; a grave sinner has no claim to honor.
rows.anchor: لا حرمة لفاسق ؛ لأنه إذا ترك حق الحق فمتى يحفظ حق الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By implication, intercession benefits those whom God permits to intercede; if He accepts anyone’s intercession, the Prophet’s and His elect’s intercession for lesser people must also be accepted.
rows.anchor: دليل الخطاب أن من أذن له في الشفاعة تنفعه الشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God allows shaykhs to intercede today for their disciples.
rows.anchor: والحق سبحانه يشفع الشيوخ في مريديهم اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet intercedes in the hereafter to raise the obedient and forgive sinners; shaykhs intercede for progressing disciples with realization and guidance, and for confused disciples with pardon.
rows.anchor: شفاعة الرسول عليه السلام غدا للمطيعين بزيادة الدرجة ، وللعاصين بغفران الزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author applies the same two forms to shaykhs: greater realization for seekers on the path and forgiveness for the confused and self-deluded.
rows.anchor: للذين هم أصحاب السلوك فبزيادة التحقيق والتوفيق ، وللذين هم أصحاب التخبط والغرة فبالتجاوز عنهم

rows.speaker: قائلهم
rows.claim: An anonymous Sufi verse depicts shaykhs visiting disciples in illness and coming to apologize when they sin.
rows.anchor: إذا مرضتم أتيناكم نعودكم . . . وتذنبون فنأتيكم ونعتذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stories of early shaykhs with disciples during periods of lapse illustrate this; shaykhly intercession occurs only through inward divine prompting, which teaches them proper courtesy.
rows.anchor: إن شفاعتهم لا تكون إلا بتعريف من قبل الله في الباطن ، ويكون ذلك أدبا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “by it” may refer either to what lies before and behind creation or to God Himself.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يعود إلى ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ، ويحتمل أن يعود إلى الحق - سبحانه -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Salaf’s approach is that God knows creation but creation does not encompass Him, just as He is seen but not apprehended.
rows.anchor: يعلم الخلق ولا يحيط به العلم ، كما قالوا : إنه يرى ولا يدرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creatures submit to God’s judgment and even mighty rulers bow; whoever commits injustice remains in darkness in proportion to it.
rows.anchor: ذلت له الرقاب واستسلم لحكمه الخلق ، وخضعت له الجبابرة ، ومن اقترف الظلم بقي في ظلماته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A righteous deed is one fit for acceptance, and its doer is free of impediments that obstruct its true reality.
rows.anchor: العمل الصالح ما يصلح للقبول ، وفاعله هو المتجرد عن الآفات الواقفة لحقيقة الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A righteous deed is also one for which its doer does not hasten to demand a reward.
rows.anchor: العمل الصالح ما لم يستعجل عليه صاحبه أجرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “While he is a believer” means that he remains a believer in the final state as in the present one.
rows.anchor: أي في المآل كما هو مؤمن في الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer trusts that God gives by grace, not as payment owed for faith; faith is a sign of the gift, not its cause.
rows.anchor: إيمانه أمارة لذلك لا موجب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God followed one proof with another, sent messenger after messenger, and warned people through varied instruction and many signs.
rows.anchor: أتبعنا دليلا بعد دليل ، وبعثنا رسولا بعد رسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s majesty means His glory, exaltation, praise, elevation, grandeur, and entitlement to attributes of majesty.
rows.anchor: وكبرياؤه : سناؤه وعلاه ومجده ورفعته وعظمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing the basmala instills awe and spiritual absence; verified encounter strengthens the heart, and when the lower self and its misgivings fall silent, the heart voices its unveilings.
rows.anchor: فإذا خرست النفوس ، وزالت هواجسها ، فالقلوب تنطق بما تكاشف به من الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the path of knowledge, one first learns and then chooses to act; what comes from God occurs first and is understood afterward, yet the recipient remains willing though its cause is obscure.
rows.anchor: الذي طريقه العلم يعلم صاحبه أولا ثم يعمل مختارا ، وما كان من الحق يجري ويحصل ثم بعده يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Different people receive different benefits: protection from calamity, joyful expansion, sweetness of obedience, or intimacy in their breaths.
rows.anchor: فلأقوام بركات في دفع البلايا عن نفوسهم وعن أموالهم ، ولآخرين في لذاذات بسطهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sacred laws differ in practical dealings but agree in fundamental knowledge; people also differ between intensified obligations and promises and eased obligations and promises.
rows.anchor: الشرائع مختلفة فيما كان من المعاملات ، متفقة فيما كان من جملة المعارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God over provision includes recognizing His bestowal in gratitude and recognizing that He accepts and rewards the worship He enables.
rows.anchor: معرفتهم إنعام الله بذلك عليهم . . . وذلك من حيث الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To submit to the one God is to accept His judgment without inward grimace or resistance; Islam can mean sincerity, which successively purifies deeds, character, states, and breaths.
rows.anchor: استسلموا لحكمه بلا تعبيس ولا استكراه من داخل القلب . والإسلام يكون بمعنى الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritually humble persist in obedience with uprightness as far as able, showing full submission and lasting reverence through lowering the inner self.
rows.anchor: الإخبات استدامة الطاعة بشرط الاستقامة بقدر الاستطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearts tremble at remembrance from fear of punishment, a bad final outcome, dying heedless and unprepared, or shame before God for disapproved acts done under His gaze.
rows.anchor: إما لخوف عقوبة ستحصل أو لمخافة عاقبة بالسوء تختم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart’s trembling corresponds to divine disclosure; during witnessing and unveiling, hearts are characterized by awe.
rows.anchor: الوجل على حسب تجلي الحق للقلب ؛ فإن القلوب في حال المطالعة والتجلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trembling may have a cause, such as fear of one’s shortcomings, or no cause and belong to awe; fear of divine stratagem is also trembling, and the closest heart fears God most.
rows.anchor: وجل له سبب وجل بلا سبب ؛ فالأول مخافة من تقصير ، والثاني معدود في جملة الهيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient remain quiet under the course of divine decree, neither resisting nor wishing escape or relief, and surrender willingly.
rows.anchor: خامدين تحت جريان الحكم من غير استكراه ولا تمني خرجة ، ولا زوم فرجة بل يستسلم طوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading of patience is guarding one’s inner secrets instead of seeking comfort by showing one’s condition to people.
rows.anchor: الحافظين معه أسرارهم ، لا يطلبون السلوة بإطلاع الخلق على أحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When affliction intensifies, they seek refuge in standing before God in intimate prayer.
rows.anchor: إذا اشتدت بهم البلوى فزعوا إلى الوقوف في محل النجوى

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: An unattributed couplet says that while others wish for rest, the speaker wishes to complain to God and be heard.
rows.anchor: إذا ما تمنى الناس روحا وراحة . . . تمنيت أن أشكو إليك فتسمعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They give their money in ordinary dealings and, in spiritual trial, surrender themselves and all they have to the demands of destiny.
rows.anchor: وفي قضايا المنازلة بالاستسلام ، وتسليم النفس وكل ما منك وبك لطوارق التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They spend their bodies bearing the demands of sacred law and their hearts by yielding to the demands of spiritual reality.
rows.anchor: فينفقون أبدانهم على تحمل مطالبات الشريعة ، وينفقون قلوبهم على التسليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sacrificial animals benefit people through riding, carrying, milk, meat, wool, and reflection on how their powerful forms are subjected to human use.
rows.anchor: أقسام الخير فيها كثيرة بالركوب والحمل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their strength and form notwithstanding, even children can make them kneel for loading or riding; they bear travel thirst and little fodder, and are soothed by the camel-driver’s chant.
rows.anchor: ثم كيف تنقاد للصبييان في البروك عند الحمل عليها وركوبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After slaughter, feed the needy petitioner who reveals his poverty and the needy visitor who keeps it concealed.
rows.anchor: القانع الذي ألقى جلباب الحياء وأظهر فقره للناس ، والمعتر الذي هو في تحمله متحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Physical, financial, or mixed acts are not accepted for their outward form alone; sincerity must accompany them and remove regard for other people.
rows.anchor: العبرة باقترانها بالإخلاص فإذا انصاف إلى أكساب الجوارح إخلاص القصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God-consciousness is witnessing God’s uniqueness, with no attention to anyone else in worship and no payment taken from people for one’s work.
rows.anchor: التقوى شهود الحق بنعت التفرد ؛ فلا يشاب تقربك بملاحظة أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s greatness for guidance means He guided people to fulfill the rights of servanthood according to sacred law.
rows.anchor: هداكم وأرشدكم إلى القيام بحق العبودية على قضية الشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsan is worshipping God as though seeing Him; its soundness shows when nothing feels burdensome or wearisome to the heart.
rows.anchor: أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repels Satan’s promptings from their breasts, sinful thoughts from their hearts, and forgetfulness from their spirits.
rows.anchor: يدفع عن صدورهم نزغات الشيطان ، وعن قلوبهم خطرات العصيان ، وعن أرواحهم طوارق النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treachery may concern wealth, deeds, or spiritual states: deeds are betrayed by ostentation, while states are betrayed by self-regard, conceit, and complacency; conceit is worst and mere self-regard most hidden.
rows.anchor: فخيانة الأعمال بالرياء والتصنع ، وخيانة الأحوال بالملاحظة والإعجاب والمساكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection, limbs testify against people without choice, but can also testify for them: an eye says it looked through them and also that it wept through them.
rows.anchor: تشهد عليهم أعضاؤهم بما عملوا من غير اختيار منهم ، ثم كما تشهد بعض أعضائهم عليهم تشهد بعض أعضائهم لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Limb testimony is deferred until the resurrection, but signs of love appear now in pallor, wasting, tears, and a fluttering heart.
rows.anchor: شهادة الأعضاء في القيامة مؤجلة ، وشهادتها في المحبة اليوم معجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards worshippers with gardens and recompense for their works, while gnostics receive union and nearness for purifying their states; the former gain high ranks and the latter intimate visions and communion.
rows.anchor: للعابدين بالجنان والمثوبة على توفية أعمالهم ، وللعارفين بالوصلة والقربة على تصفية أحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of God becomes necessary experiential certainty, freeing them from reasoning and recollection and ending the heart’s fluctuation because inner insight suffices.
rows.anchor: فتصير المعرفة ضرورية ؛ فيجدون المعافاة من النظر وتذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the hereafter they witness only the Real and stand through, for, and with Him, who discloses their mysteries and realities.
rows.anchor: لا يشهدون غدا إلا الحق ؛ فهم قائمون بالحق للحق مع الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Impure women” may mean forbidden deeds, matched to men who willingly choose them; each deed and doer suits the other in purity, baseness, or honor.
rows.anchor: من الأعمال وهي المحظورات { للخبيثين } : من الرجال المؤثرين لها طوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes the impure things states, pleasures, wishes, and desires belonging to those who pursue them; each quality stays with its matching person.
rows.anchor: من الأحوال ؛ وهي الحظوظ والمنى والشهوات لأصحابها والساعين لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Impure things can also be lowly objects matched to people content with low stations, as carrion is food for dogs.
rows.anchor: من الأشياء للخبيثين من الأشخاص وهم الراضون بالمنازل السحيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Impure things may be unlawful earnings suited to men whose rank and aspiration settle on them, while such wealth gravitates to such men.
rows.anchor: من الأموال - وهي التي ليست بحلال - لمن بها رتبته ، وعليها تعتكف همته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pure things are acts of obedience and nearness, and pure people are those who prefer and pursue them.
rows.anchor: من الأعمال هي الطاعات والقرب للطيبين والطيبون هم المؤثرون لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun of the day sets at night, but the sun of hearts never sets; its light and rising are even fuller at night.
rows.anchor: شمس النهار تغرب بالليل . . . وشمس القلوب ليست تغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Times are alike, but worship and reward are greater at some times; night and day compensate for defects in each other’s worship.
rows.anchor: فمن وقع له في طاعة الليل خلل فإذا حضر بالنهار فذلك وجود جبرانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deserve the Merciful’s mercy are enabled to obey by that mercy; by His mercy they reach obedience, and by their obedience they reach Paradise.
rows.anchor: وبطاعتهم وصلوا إلى جنته . . . هكذا لسان الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Humbly” means with humility and reverence; humility requires never admiring one’s own states, works, or spiritual condition.
rows.anchor: متواضعين متخاشعين . ويقال شرط التواضع وحده ألا يستحسن شيئا من أحواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When ignorant people address them, they speak rightly; they answer insults with praise, slander with gentleness and good speech, and reassure the harsh that they are safe from retaliation.
rows.anchor: قالوا سلاما } : قيل سداد المنطق ؛ ويقال من خاطبهم بالقدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They spend nights prostrating and wake with spiritual finding, the fruit of their souls’ prostration; abundant night prayer beautifies one’s face by day through honor before God.
rows.anchor: يبيتون لربهم ساجدين ، ويصبحون واجدين ؛ فوجد صباحهم ثمرات سجود أرواحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their outward beauty comes through prostration and their inward beauty through spiritual finding, while they observe the manners of existence.
rows.anchor: أحسن الأشياء ظاهر بالسجود محسن وباطن بالوجود مزين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They strive to their utmost yet place themselves, when asking God, among sinners who apologize and disavow their claims.
rows.anchor: يجتهدون غاية الاجتهاد ، ويستفرغون نهاية الوسع ، وعند السؤال ينزلون منزلة العصاة

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: An unattributed couplet says the speaker approached only after taking the posture of a humiliated servant.
rows.anchor: وما رمت الدخول عليه حتى . . . حللت محلة العبد الذليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Extravagance means spending on desire and the ego’s share; spending for God is not extravagance, while miserliness means withholding from God.
rows.anchor: الإسراف أن تنفق في الهوى وفي نصيب النفس ، فأما ما كان لله فليس فيه إسراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting one’s own spending to prevent following desires and to become accustomed to little is not blameworthy miserliness.
rows.anchor: التضييق على النفس منعا لها عن اتباع الشهوات ولتتعود الاجتراء باليسير فليس بالاقتار المذموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ flight can be read literally as fear for his life; fleeing when one lacks the power to resist is not blameworthy.
rows.anchor: يجوز حمله على ظاهره ، وأنه خاف منهم على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that Moses feared God’s punishment would descend on them because of their idolatry, or fled in response to Pharaoh’s claim to be their only god.
rows.anchor: خفت أن تنزل بكم عقوبة من الله لشؤم شرككم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh counted sparing Moses’ life among the Israelites as a favor, but Moses rejects this: enslaving the Israelites is no kindness and gives Pharaoh no claim over him.
rows.anchor: هل استعبادك لبني إسرائيل يعد نعمة ؟ إن ذلك ليس بنعمة ، ولا لك فيها منة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s ignorant question uses “what,” a term for the nonrational; Moses ignores its wording and describes God as the deity of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: فسأل بلفظ { ما } - و ( ما ) يستخبر بها عما لا يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses answers Pharaoh by describing God as the Lord of Pharaoh and his earliest ancestors.
rows.anchor: قال موسى : { ربكم ورب ءابآئكم الأولين } فحاد فرعون عن سنن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh abandons proper discourse for foolishness; Moses refuses to engage the insult and answers as one would address people capable of reason and discernment.
rows.anchor: فحاد فرعون عن سنن الاستقامة في الخطاب ، وأخذ في السفاهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: لئن اتخذت إلها غيري لأجعلنك من المسجونين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ staff became a serpent that nearly swallowed Pharaoh’s palace and its occupants; Pharaoh fled trembling, hid under his throne, was exposed, and begged Moses for protection before God returned it to a staff.
rows.anchor: وقلبها - سبحانه - ثعبانا كاد يلتقم دار فرعون بمن فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Moses left, Pharaoh’s unbelief returned; he gathered his people, who agreed Moses had bewitched them, then summoned the sorcerers despite the sign.
rows.anchor: فجمع قومه وكلمهم في أمره ، وأجمعوا كلهم على أنه سحرهم

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: An unattributed saying compares Pharaoh’s return to error with a sick person relapsing after seeming to recover.
rows.anchor: إذا ارعوى عاد إلى جهله . . . كذي الضنى عاد إلى نكسه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The letter was considered noble because it began with the basmala.
rows.anchor: لأنه كان مصدرا ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation of its nobility is that it named God first rather than using a sender-and-recipient formula such as “from Solomon to so-and-so.”
rows.anchor: كتب فيه اسم نفسه أولا ولم يقل : إنه من سليمان إلى فلانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the letter sought no worldly kingship but called the queen to God and to submit.
rows.anchor: لم يكن في الكتاب ذكر الطمع في الملك بل كان دعاء إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter seized the queen’s heart; by honoring it as noble, she preserved her kingdom, received Islam, and gained Solomon’s companionship.
rows.anchor: فلما عرفت قدر الكتاب وصلت باحترامها إلى بقاء ملكها ، ورزقت الإسلام وصحبة سليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the letter is noble because it contains the basmala, prayer is noble when it retains the naming formula and deficient when stripped of it.
rows.anchor: فالكريم من الصلاة ما لا يتجرد عن التسمية . وإذا تجردت كان الأمر فيها بالعكس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen consulted others on a grave matter; a ruler should not decide alone but should consult people of judgment and insight.
rows.anchor: فإن الملك لا ينبغي أن يكون مستبدا برأيه ، ويجب أن يكون له قوم من أهل الرأي والبصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counselors answer courteously: they can exert their strength, offer sincere advice, and carry out the decision, while the command belongs to the queen.
rows.anchor: ليس منا إلا بذل الوسع ، وليس لنا إلا إظهار النصح وما علينا إلا متابعة الأمر

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: One view assigns “Thus do they act” to the queen’s own speech.
rows.anchor: ويقال إن : { وكذلك يفعلون } من قولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A just ruler entering a town removes injustice and establishes justice, whereas an unjust ruler removes what is good and installs falsehood.
rows.anchor: فإن كان الداخل عادلا أزال سنة الجور ، وأثبت سنة العدل ، وإن كان الداخل جائرا أزال الحسن وأثبت الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misrule ruins lands when low people dominate the noble; sound rulers rescue the honorable from the base and raise justice.
rows.anchor: فإن خراب البلاد بولاة السوء ، حيث يستولي أسافل الناس وأسقاطهم على الأعزة منهم

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: An unattributed poem laments a state with no trace of nobility and says it has become a burden on the honorable.
rows.anchor: يا دولة ليس فيها . . . من المعالي شظيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The social image also describes spiritual renovation: recognition and virtuous traits expel desire and vile qualities, replacing them with noble states that complete a person’s happiness.
rows.anchor: المعرفة والخصال المحمودة إذا باشرت قلب عبد أخرجت عنه الشهوات والمنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When base ego and blameworthy traits take over the heart, they ruin its spiritual home and virtues, multiplying affliction.
rows.anchor: متى استولت على قلب غاغة النفس والخصال المذمومة أزالت عنه عمارته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The allusion of the moving mountains applies to spiritually established people who are outwardly settled among others but inwardly journey through the heavenly realm.
rows.anchor: ساكنون بنفوسهم سائحون في الملكوت بأسرارهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The gnostic is present with people outwardly yet absent from all creation in his innermost being.
rows.anchor: العارف كائن بائن ؛ كائن مع الناس بظاهره ، بائن عن جميع الخلق بسرائره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Good” may be an intensive term, or mean a share of good, a good outcome, or reward better than the good already possessed.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون { خير } ها هنا للمبالغة ؛ لأن الذي له في الآخرة من الثواب خير مما منه من القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who come with good are safe from the terror of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وهم آمنون من فزع القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who come with evil face the opposite outcome from the obedient: as their present state differs, so their hereafter judgment is contrary.
rows.anchor: فكما أن حالهم اليوم من المطيعين بالعكس فحكمهم غدا في الآخرة بالضد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was commanded to follow the upright religion, disavow overt and hidden association, and remain on the straight path.
rows.anchor: أمره بالدين الحنيفي ، والتبري من الشرك ؛ الجلي منه والخفي ، وبملازمة الطريق السوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guarantees His protection and due to whoever follows and believes in the Messenger.
rows.anchor: من اتبعه وصدقه أوجب الحق ذمامه وحقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will soon show people His signs; blessed is the one who turns back before death, and woe to the one who turns back after the opportunity has passed.
rows.anchor: سيريكم - عن قريب - آياته ، فطوبى لمن رجع قبل وفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ sister offered a family to nurse him; they accepted from compassion, returned him to his mother, and he nursed contentedly, so they called her his caretaker and wet nurse.
rows.anchor: قالت لهم أخته : { هل أدلكم على أهل بيت يكفلونه لكم } ؟ فقبلوا نصيحتها شفقة منهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Egyptians called Moses’ mother his nurse and caretaker without harming her, while calling Pharaoh his father did him no good.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يدعون أمه حاضنة ومرضعة . . ولم يضرها ، وكانوا يقولون عن فرعون : إنه أبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Moses matured, God gave him judgment by completing his preparation and granting him knowledge; this is God’s way with the eminent and prophets.
rows.anchor: لما كملت سنه وتم عقله ، واستوى كمال خصاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses entered at midday while people were dispersed; he found an Israelite follower fighting an Egyptian opponent, and the Israelite asked him for help.
rows.anchor: دخل المدينة في وقت الهاجرة ، وتفرق الناس ، فوجد فيها رجلين يتخاصمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses struck the Egyptian to push him away from the Israelite, without intending to kill him, but the man died from the blow.
rows.anchor: فوكزه موسى ليدفعه عن الإسرائيلي ، فمات الرجل بذلك الوكز ، ولم يكن موسى يقصد قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses called the harsh blow Satan’s work; he did not attribute the killing itself to Satan, but wished he had pushed the man more gently because Satan prompted his severity.
rows.anchor: ولم ينسب القتل إلى الشيطان ، ولكن دفعه عنه بالغلظة نسبه إلى الشيطان بأن حمله على تلك الحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God wills an outcome, He creates its causes; the Egyptian’s death from one blow fulfilled the decree, since many blows and lashes may leave someone alive.
rows.anchor: إذا أراده الله أمرا أجرى أسبابا ليحصل بها مراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses repented and sought forgiveness; God said He forgave him, so there is no reproach after forgiveness.
rows.anchor: تاب موسى عما جرى على يده ، واستغفر ربه ، وأخبر الله أنه غفر له ، ولا عتاب بعد المغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses acknowledged God’s favor in enabling his repentance and vowed not to repeat his former act.
rows.anchor: رب بما أنعمت علي من توفيقك لي بالتوبة فلن أعود بعد ذلك إلى مثل ما سلف مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses feared Pharaoh would accuse him of intentional murder despite claiming justice, and watched for news of discovery.
rows.anchor: فهو { يترقب } علم فرعون وأن يخبر بذلك في وقته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations say Moses feared God over what he had done, feared punishment would fall on his people, awaited God’s help, or waited for a companion to comfort him.
rows.anchor: من الله مما جرى منه . ويقال { خآئفا } على قومه حلول العذاب بهم
